statement: You are given an infix expression, expression, in which each operator sits between its two operands and parentheses may group sub-expressions. Operands are single uppercase letters A to Z. The operators are +, −, *, / and ^, all binary.

Convert it to postfix notation, where each operator comes after its two operands and no parentheses are needed. Use the usual precedence: ^ binds tightest, then * and /, then + and −. Operators of equal precedence group left to right, except ^, which groups right to left.
Return the postfix expression as a string with no spaces.

examples.explanation: B*C is evaluated first, then A is added to it, then D is subtracted, giving A B C * + D −.
The parentheses make both sums happen before the multiplication, so * comes last.
